A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Obliviator paper, with readable main text and complete Appendices A–F. Comparing all pages establishes that differences are confined to Figure 4(b) and the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-erasure experiments, utility-erasure curves, fairness measurements, computational measurements, and ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and replaces the reported DIAL-SENTIMENT plot in Figure 4(b).

M1.justification: The HSIC-based encoder objective, iterative RKHS refinement, and training procedure remain identical in Section 4 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions cover BIAS IN BIOS, DIAL-MENTION, and DIAL-SENTIMENT with the same tasks and scenarios. Figure 4(b) replaces a plot for an already documented evaluation.

E2.justification: Figure 4(b) retains FaRM, KRaM, INLP, and kSAL as comparators. Comparator membership in all other main-text and appendix experiments is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, model configurations, training settings, metrics, and probing procedures are unchanged. Figure 4(b) still represents the existing frozen-BERT, unsupervised DIAL-SENTIMENT evaluation; its corrected axis label does not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: The probing-network comparisons, single-step versus multi-step ablation, sampling-skew analysis, hyperparameter sensitivity studies, fairness analyses, and visualizations are identical.

E5.justification: Run and seed descriptions, maximum-over-probes aggregation, and timing uncertainty reporting remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices B–C.

E6.justification: In v1, Figure 4(b) duplicates the DIAL-MENTION curves and baseline points from Figure 4(a). v2 replaces them with distinct DIAL-SENTIMENT trajectories and comparator coordinates; the chance reference shifts from approximately 50%/50% to 63%/54% race/task accuracy. Other reported results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The dependence measures, mathematical assumptions, optimization formulations, and derivations and proofs in Appendix A are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about nonlinear guardedness, utility-erasure trade-offs, and generalization across language models.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning label visibility, representation disentanglement, sampling skew, and fairness are unchanged. Appendices E–F retain the same limitations and applicability cautions.

D1.justification: Implementation instructions, encoder architecture, hyperparameters, hardware, computational measurements, probing specifications, and code-access information are identical.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning, citations, and all 33 reference entries are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 8 March 2026 to v2 dated 29 April 2026. The paper's prose, headings, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4(b) is redrawn with different curves, baseline points, and axis ticks, and its vertical label changes from 'Mention Acc.' to 'Sentiment Acc.' Its caption and placement, all other figures and tables, and the surrounding layout remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the obvious duplication of the DIAL-MENTION plot under the DIAL-SENTIMENT caption in Figure 4(b), providing a distinct sentiment comparison with an appropriate task label. This improves the accuracy and usefulness of one main experimental panel. The rest of the paper, including its appendices, is unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
